content:
Whole numbers look easy — until the Olympiad asks which property justifies a step, or what division by zero means. This chapter is about the STRUCTURE of arithmetic. Here is what the IMO Class 6 whole numbers chapter tests, with a free 10-question test.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Whole Numbers chapter tests

  • Whole numbers, successors and predecessors on the number line
  • Commutative, associative and identity properties
  • Distributivity for smart mental maths
  • Number patterns and division facts

Key facts your child should know

  • 0 is a whole number but not a natural number.
  • a × (b + c) = ab + ac — the distributive law powers tricks like 104 × 25.
  • a + 0 = a and a × 1 = a (identities); a × 0 = 0.
  • Division by zero is undefined.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Assuming subtraction and division are commutative.
  • Giving 0 a predecessor in whole numbers.
  • Writing a ÷ 0 = 0 instead of undefined.

questions.q: Using the distributive property, simplify: 35 x 98 + 35 x 2
On a number line, A is at 24 and B is at 58. What number is exactly midway between A and B?
What number is obtained by finding the predecessor 6 times starting from 3991?
A number when divided by 7 gives quotient 245 and remainder 3. Find the number.
questions.explanation: Number = Divisor x Quotient + Remainder = 7 x 245 + 3 = 1718.

questions.q: A number leaves remainder 5 when divided by 8 and remainder 3 when divided by 5. What is the smallest such number?
questions.explanation: 13 / 8 = 1 R5 and 13 / 5 = 2 R3. The smallest such number is 13.

faq.q: Is every natural number a whole number?
faq.a: Yes — the whole numbers are the naturals plus zero. So every natural is whole, but 0 is whole and not natural.
Multiplication distributes over addition: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c. It lets you compute 104 × 25 as 2600 + 100.
